newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia rupiah stable, short-term swaps well bid.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia rupiah stable, short-term swaps well bid.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in late trade on Tuesday, dealers said.
They said volume was thin in a lethargic market, with the focus still on liquidity. Overnight money was last at 14.0 percent after briefly easing to 12.5 percent.
One state bank dealer said weekly tax payments due Tuesday posed no problem to the market, but operators remained cautious in anticipation of Friday's amount which was likely to be larger.
"There is no drive in the market," one U.S. bank dealer said, adding that the market was directionless.
Dealers said rates hovered between 2,427.0 and 2,428.5 throughout the day.
Spot rupiah was last at 2,428.00/28.25 at 0800 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,427.0/28.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,427.5/27.75 and 2,426.75/27.00, respectively.

Dealers explained the lethargy in the market to expensive short-dated swaps which prevented operators from taking long dollar positions. Some dealers said going long on dollars was justified because of political concerns over the ongoing campaign for the May 29 general elections.

The U.S. bank dealer said tom/next swaps were supported. One currency dealer in Singapore said earlier the market was short in the forward market while long on dollars on the spot side, reflected by continuous high tom/next swap rates.
But he was not sure whether it was advisable to take on a long dollar/short forward position because the rupiah had not depreciated fast enough to facilitate such a move.
Overnight swap was at 0.60/0.65 and tom/next at 0.45/0.50.
One-month swaps were at 13.75/14.50, two at 26.25/27.00, three at 38.5/39.5 and six at 78.0/78.5 points.

The central bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,407/2,599 and the conversion band also by one point to 2,407/2,455 on Tuesday after lowering them by one point each in the past two trading days.
